found_by: the in-process fuzzer, read-write mode, on the seed built to carry an unreplayed journal
base: an early version of Tests/fuzz/make_seeds.sh seed s06, whose recipe staged /dev/urandom for journal blocks 1, 2 and 3

edits.what: a committed journal transaction staging arbitrary bytes for block 1, which on a 1 KiB volume is the superblock

symptom: jbd_recover replays the log by block number, reloads the superblock afterwards (patch 0023, correctly, so the flag edits that follow do not run on a stale copy), and then believes what it loaded. s_log_block_size came back as 955747801 and the next thing the code did was shift by it: ext4_super.h:95, 'shift exponent 955747801 is too large for 32-bit type int'. The flag edits below would then have written that superblock back over the medium with RECOVER cleared.
note: The seed recipe was the bug's discoverer and its cause. s06 now stages inode-table blocks with their own current contents, so replay is a no-op that still has to be performed; this image keeps the hostile version.
fixed_by: patches/lwext4/0066-a-journal-that-replays-a-superblock-is-not-to-be-believed.patch, plus a re-probe after replay in ext4b_mount (Core/shim/ext4_bridge.c)
reproduce: build/bin/ext4dump mkdir /x (any write verb forces a read-write mount, which replays)
